findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed creamer dispenser did not have a drip tray, so liquid creamer was dripping straight onto the counter. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the drip tray was located, put in place, and drips were cleaned up. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of an accumulation of residue.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the mop sink caulking is molding and starting to deteriorate. The caulking must be replaced/repaired to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the mop sink caulking is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the blue container holding clean utensils by the sandwich prep cooler has an accumulation of food debris on the bottom. The container must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid contaminating food contact surfaces. The PIC removed the container to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that the container is maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that there is an accumulation of dust on the drink shelves in the walk-in cooler. The shelves must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there are small holes in the wall in the following locations: (1) Around the hand sink across from the sandwich prep cooler; (2) To the right of the triple sink; and (3) Around the hand sink by the kitchen entrance. Ensure that the holes are filled to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a CFPM at the facility upon inspection. There always needs be a CFPM at the facility during operational hours. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket when the inspectors arrived at the facility. The facility was operating and cooking pizza’s when the inspectors arrived. An employee created a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure there is a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop head sitting in the water of a mop bucket and several mops siting with the heads on the ground in the mop sink. When the PIC was asked, he stated that the mop bucket was not currently in use. Mops should always be placed in a position that allows them to air dry. This is a repeat violation from 12/11/2023. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Two employees were actively working in the kitchen during the inspection. One staff member washed hands one time. The other staff member did not wash hands at all despite repeatedly switching from cleaning to food preparation throughout the inspection AND returning from smoking. Hand washing MUST BE occurring frequently to prevent contamination of foods in the facility. A discussion was held with operator who will discuss with staff the importance of hand washing. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Two mop heads were observed to be store on the ground during the inspection. Soiled mop heads must immediately be taken to laundry if ready to be laundered. In-use mops must be stored with their heads in the upper portion of the mop bucket or hanging inverted along the wall to prevent contamination and facilitate air drying. Ensure that mops are stored properly at all times. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed 4-5 flies throughout the pizza prep area. There is a fly trap on the wall away from food prep, but it does not appear to be working to attract pests more frequently. Suggested fly strip placed away from food prep areas. Inspector will follow-up on 7/27/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee entered the kitchen and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to begin food prep. Employee was advised on handwashing upon entering the kitchen and prior to putting on gloves to work with food. Hands were washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for the remainder of inspection.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the work area, prior to donning gloves, and after any activities that may contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer solution in sani-bucket at front counter was at 0ppm quat. Manager was preparing to change sanitizer solution in the kitchen and prepared fresh solutions for both sani-buckets. Proper concentration was observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration. Consider pre-soaking wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths. Also, allow solution to run several seconds prior to filling sani-buckets to ensure chemical is properly suctioning through the chemical line.

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 C Vegetable wash was not registering at proper range for dilution. Per the product use directions, a range of 0.75-1.0 (dilution 1:170 to 1:128) is required. When dispensed for testing, the solution did not register a color on the range indicated for the corresponding test strips chart. A call for service will be made. In the meantime, fruits and vegetables will need to be rinsed at a prep sink until vegetable wash is registering at proper range for use. 
Devices used for on-site generation of chemicals meeting the requirements specified in 21 CFR 173.315, Chemicals used in the washing or to assist in the peeling of fruits and vegetables, for the washing of raw, whole fruits and vegetables shall be used in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed self-service tongs to be placed in area soiled with food debris. Observed "clean" equipment to be setting in soiled area. Ensure all equipment is cleaned as needed as well as placed in clean areas. Corrected. PIC ensures equipment will be cleaned. Reference 4-601.11(A).
